jarPolymerMaterials.name: Polycarbonate (PC - Bisphenol-A Polycondensate)
jarPolymerMaterials.description: Standard transparent shatter-resistant plastic used in high-performance blenders manufactured prior to 2013–2015 and widely used in commercial catering jugs. The carbonate ester linkages (-O-C(=O)-O-) undergo rapid hydrolytic cleavage when exposed to aqueous liquids above 60°C or alkaline dishwasher cycles, depolymerizing back into free Bisphenol-A.

jarPolymerMaterials.name: Eastman Tritan™ Copolyester (TX1001 / TX2001)
jarPolymerMaterials.estrogenicPotency: Low-to-Undetected (Potential non-BPA cyclic oligomer migration under high heat)
jarPolymerMaterials.description: Engineered copolyester synthesized to replace polycarbonate in premium blenders (Vitamix, Ninja, Blendtec). While free of Bisphenol-A and phthalates, continuous thermal exposure (>85°C) and dishwasher alkali stress cause micro-crazing and leaching of low-molecular-weight cyclic ester oligomers and TMCD derivatives.

jarPolymerMaterials.name: Styrene Acrylonitrile Resin (SAN)
jarPolymerMaterials.description: Rigid, clear, but highly brittle polymer common in entry-level blenders and budget food processors. Prone to severe mechanical micro-fissuring and crazing upon repeated ice crushing. Releases residual styrene monomer when exposed to high temperatures and lipophilic oils.

jarPolymerMaterials.name: Tempered Borosilicate Glass (Non-Polymer Control)
jarPolymerMaterials.description: Heavy mineral silicate glass resistant to thermal shocks up to 150°C. Contains zero synthetic organic polymers, plasticizers, bisphenols, or cyclic oligomers. 100% chemically impervious to acid hydrolysis and oil extraction.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Boiling Acidic Soup (Tomato / Squash Puree)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Boiling liquids (>85°C) placed directly into a blender jar trigger aggressive ester bond hydrolysis along the jar interior walls. Acidity (pH < 4.0) acts as an acid catalyst, dramatically increasing cleavage rates of ester and carbonate linkages.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Frozen Berry & Citrus Smoothie with Crushed Ice
foodMatrixProfiles.description: High acidity (citric, malic, ascorbic acids) combined with high-hardness crystalline ice particles. The violent impact of ice shards at 25,000+ RPM inflicts microscopic mechanical pitting and microcracks across the lower third of the jar.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Warm Roasted Peanut / Almond Butter Emulsion
foodMatrixProfiles.description: High-fat food matrices serve as powerful non-polar organic solvents. Hydrophobic additives, plasticizer phthalates, and bisphenol monomers partition preferentially out of the polymer matrix directly into the lipid triglyceride phase.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Cold Whey Protein Milkshake (Water/Milk Base)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Near-neutral aqueous emulsion at room temperature. Minimal thermal or chemical thermodynamic driving force for polymer chain cleavage, providing an empirical baseline.

blenderSpeedMechanics.name: Ultra-High Speed Commercial Motor (30,000 RPM / ~82 m/s Tip Speed)
blenderSpeedMechanics.description: Commercial-grade blenders (Vitamix Pro, Blendtec Stealth, Waring Commercial). Extreme blade velocity creates hydrodynamic cavitation pockets; microscopic bubble implosions generate localized micro-jets (>1000 bar) that erode the inner jar surface.

blenderSpeedMechanics.name: Standard High-Speed Blender (16,000 RPM / ~44 m/s Tip Speed)
blenderSpeedMechanics.description: Typical mid-range residential countertop blender. Generates substantial fluid shear and moderate cavitation, sufficient to accelerate mass transfer of leached substances across boundary layers.

blenderSpeedMechanics.name: Low Speed / Pulse Agitation (8,000 RPM / ~22 m/s Tip Speed)
blenderSpeedMechanics.description: Gentle stirring and emulsification mode. Cavitation is negligible, and mechanical kinetic energy imparted to polymer wall interfaces is minimal.

jarDegradationStates.name: Pristine Factory New (0 Dishwasher Cycles, Mirror Surface)
jarDegradationStates.description: Freshly injection-molded jar with intact surface resin skin. Low roughness and absence of micro-cavities limit exposed surface area to baseline nominal geometry.

jarDegradationStates.name: Hazed & Clouded (50+ Dishwasher Cycles, Alkaline Etching)
jarDegradationStates.description: The hallmark white/cloudy film on aged blender jars. Dishwasher detergents (pH 10–12) at 65°C chemically etch ester linkages. The resulting micro-pitting increases the contact surface area by over 300% and strips the protective outer skin.

jarDegradationStates.name: Severely Crazed (3+ Years Heavy Wear, Spiderweb Microcracks)
jarDegradationStates.description: Extensive network of microscopic cracks visible under direct light. Created by thermal shock (ice right after hot soup) and repetitive acoustic shockwaves from ice crushing. Fissures penetrate 50–200 µm into the polymer bulk, creating massive leaching channels.
